result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.simplify()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Remove all self-loops and duplicate edges, making the graph simple. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1273-L1352){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.simplify() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A simple graph has no self-loops (edges from a node to itself) and no multi-edges (multiple edges between the same pair of nodes). This method removes both types, which is a common preprocessing step for algorithms that require simple graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - equivalent to calling `remove_selfloops()` followed by `remove_duplicate_edges()` - for duplicate edges, the first edge (lowest edge ID) in each group is retained - for directed graphs, edges `(u, v)` and `(v, u)` are considered different pairs - for undirected graphs, edges `(u, v)` and `(v, u)` are considered the same pair - after simplification, `is_simple()` will return `True` ## Examples {.doc-examples} Simplify a graph with both self-loops and multi-edges: ::: {#9d3ce1f6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=2.0) # Duplicate .add_edge(source="A", target="A") # Self-loop .add_edge(source="B", target="B") # Self-loop ) # Before: 4 edges, not simple (g.count_edges(), g.is_simple()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (4, False) ``` ::: ::: After simplify: ::: {#9d9b7d7e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=2.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="A") .add_edge(source="B", target="B") .simplify() ) # Now: 1 edge, is simple (g.count_edges(), g.is_simple()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (1, True) ``` ::: ::: Use in preprocessing pipeline: ::: {#ddaed837 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_node(label="Z") .add_edge(source="X", target="Y") .add_edge(source="X", target="Y") # Duplicate .add_edge(source="Y", target="Z") .add_edge(source="Z", target="Z") # Self-loop .simplify() ) g.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
